explain.say: When you walk on firm ground, your foot pushes back on the ground and the ground pushes you forward. Almost all your push goes into moving you.

faq.q: Why is walking in sand harder?
faq.a: Loose sand grains slide away as you push off, so some of your push is wasted moving sand instead of you. Your feet also sink and must be lifted out every step.
asks: Why do my legs get tired on the beach?

faq.q: How much harder is walking on sand?
faq.a: A study in 1998 found that walking on soft sand takes about 1.6 to 2.5 times as much energy as walking on a firm surface. Running on sand costs less extra, up to about 1.6 times.
asks: Do you burn more energy walking on sand?

faq.q: Why is wet sand easier to walk on?
faq.a: In damp sand, thin films of water between the grains pull them together, making the sand firmer. It pushes back better, so less of your effort is wasted. Very wet, soupy sand is soft again.
asks: Why is sand firmer near the sea?

faq.q: How do camels walk easily on sand?
faq.a: Camels have wide, flat, padded feet that spread their weight over a big area, so they sink less. Snowshoes work the same way on soft snow.
asks: How do camels not sink in sand?

faq.q: Is walking on sand good exercise?
faq.a: Yes. Because it takes more effort, walking on sand works your leg muscles harder and uses more energy than walking the same distance on a pavement.

facts: Walking on soft sand takes about 1.6 to 2.5 times as much energy as walking on a hard surface (Lejeune and colleagues, 1998).
Damp sand is firmer than dry sand because thin water films between the grains pull them together.

quiz.say: Why is it easier to walk on damp sand by the sea than on dry, soft sand?
quiz.show: Damp sand is easier to walk on because…

options.show: Water pulls the grains together, making it firmer
options.say: Water pulls the grains together, making it firmer

quiz.why: Thin films of water between the grains hold them together, so the sand pushes back firmly instead of sliding away.

wrong.0: Temperature isn't what makes sand firm.
wrong.1: The sea doesn't push you; the firmer ground does the work.
